## Hand-run micro-benchmarks (#913, #922, #923, #1109, #1364, #1365)

Not written by the generator above: refreshed by the commands each part names (`filelog_bench_test.go`: `cd internal && go test -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkFileLogEntries -benchmem -count=3 ./service/app/consensus/`).

One question, the read side of ADR 0152 D15's "segmented log" row (#913):

> **What does a fetch of synced entries cost per entry, now that a run of one
> segment is read with one pread and parsed in place?**

Once a batch is synced, every read of its entries — a slow follower's fetch,
the apply goroutine's read back past `RecentEntriesBytes`, `Recover` and
`Inspect` — goes to the segment file. `per-entry` is the path before #913:
`readEntry`, a pread of the header then a pread of the record into a buffer of
its own, two allocations an entry. `range` is `Entries` since #913: the run's
interval, known from the segment's table of offsets (#1111: 4 bytes an
entry, the slot of 40 bytes it replaced held the record's length), read with ONE pread into one buffer, each
entry's `Data` aliasing it. The 4 096-entry row is the issue's 1 MiB fetch of
256-byte entries.

### Reproducibility envelope

> **Numbers vary across machines, and these are noisy.** They were taken while
> seven other test lanes ran on the same machine, and the page cache held the
> segment: the ns/entry columns spread by up to 2x between runs of one row.
> What travels is the shape — the syscall and allocation counts are exact,
> and the order of magnitude between the two paths holds in every run.

| Dimension | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | Apple M1 Pro, 10 cores |
| RAM | 16 GiB |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), darwin/arm64 |
| Go | go1.27.3 |
| Commit | a42d59ef5 (#913) plus the change of #1111 |
| Taken | 2026-11-12, `-count=3`, default `-benchtime` |

### Results

| Benchmark | ns/op (3 runs) | ns/entry | B/op | allocs/op | preads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `range/64` | 10 669, 15 932, 22 106 | 167, 249, 345 | 20 480 | 1 | 1 |
| `per-entry/64` | 135 076, 142 187, 141 774 | 2 112, 2 225, 2 216 | 20 992 | 128 | 128 |
| `range/4096` | 1 084 509, 1 463 573, 1 043 041 | 265, 358, 255 | 1 278 085 – 1 278 325 | 1 | 1 |
| `per-entry/4096` | 12 481 218, 19 868 417, 11 115 205 | 3 048, 4 851, 2 715 | 1 343 497 – 1 343 517 | 8 192 | 8 192 |

The preads column is counted, not timed: `TestEntriesReadASyncedRunOfOneSegmentInOnePread`
and the alloc lane's `TestEntriesOfASyncedRunAllocateTheBufferAndTheSlice`
assert it. `range` passes a reused `dst`, so its one allocation is the read's
buffer; into a nil `dst` the slice is grown once more, two allocations, which
is D15's budget (`Entries of 64 x 256 B: 1 pread, <= 2 allocs/op`).

### Reading it

- **The 1 MiB fetch** went from 8 192 syscalls and 8 192 allocations to one
  of each, and from 2.7 to 4.9 µs an entry to 0.26 to 0.36 µs: 8 to 19
  times faster in these runs.
- **64 entries** gain less per entry (the one pread's fixed cost is spread
  over fewer records) and still 6 to 13 times.
- **The bytes are the same**: one buffer of the records' aligned length
  against a buffer per record; the 512 B more of `per-entry/64` are its 64
  headers.

### Sync path of a batch (G1, #923)

ADR 0152 G1's row `Append 64 x 256 B + Sync`, `DataDirOptions.SyncPath =
SyncRWFDsync` (one `pwritev2(2)` flagged `RWF_DSYNC` per durability point)
against `SyncFdatasync` (`pwrite(2)` then `fdatasync(2)`), is measured per
device by the dm-crypt lane in ADR 0190's shape: both logs in one process on
the same filesystem, a round of 2 x 8 windows of 200 Syncs in the order A, B,
B, A, ..., ten rounds, and the gate held on the distribution-free interval of
the ten ratios B / A (2nd and 9th order statistics):
`testdata/dmcrypt/run.sh 12 0 <ext4|xfs> zerofill rwfdsync`,
`TestDMCryptSyncPathBench`, its `SYNCPATH` and `SYNCPATH_GATE` lines. A mode
may become the default on a device only if its entries/s ratio's lower bound
is >= 1.00 and its Sync p99 ratio's upper bound is <= 1.00.

Ten rounds a filesystem on devbox on 2026-11-13 (Debian 13, Linux 6.12.101
amd64, 8 cores; a privileged debian:stable-slim container, LUKS2
aes-xts-plain64 over a 4 GiB loop image on the host's ext4 disk), the
`SYNCPATH_GATE` lines of `testdata/dmcrypt/RESULTS.md`, "Sync path". Both
intervals straddle 1.00 on both filesystems; the suite, its fuzz seeds and
12 of 12 power cuts pass with every log writing `RWF_DSYNC`. The OVH VPS is
not measured. `SyncFdatasync` stays the default everywhere until a row
meets the gate.

The three devbox rows without dm-crypt were taken on 2026-11-13 (#1366)
on every filesystem of this host its user can write to, nothing mounted or
tuned for the run: the same test, ten rounds each, `DMCRYPT_DIR` on the
filesystem and `DMCRYPT_RUNTIME_DIR` outside `/run` (no root), e.g.
`DMCRYPT_DIR=<dir> DMCRYPT_RUNTIME_DIR=<dir> DMCRYPT_FS=ext4 go test -tags dmcrypt -run '^TestDMCryptSyncPathBench$' -v ./service/app/consensus/`.
The host's xfs, btrfs, LUKS, LVM, RAID 1, vfat and zfs mounts are not
writable to it and were not measured. Every interval straddles 1.00, the
p99 ratio's by far the most: no filesystem here lets `RWF_DSYNC` become a
default, so the io_uring mode, the smaller gain #923 lists, is not built;
it has no number of its own, because it does not exist to be measured.

### The apply side: applied1 (#1109)

From `applied_bench_test.go`; refresh with `cd internal && go test -run='^$' -bench=BenchmarkApplied1 -benchmem -benchtime=1s ./service/app/consensus/`.

The apply side of `Propose -> applied` (ADR 0152 D15): `applied1` runs once
per applied entry on the apply goroutine. Its cost must not grow with what
waits on it — the parked `Barrier` and `WaitApplied` callers, released from a
min-heap only when their index is reached — nor with an outstanding forward,
whose result is kept in a fixed ring of 4 096 slots (#1109). The race-off
alloc lane holds the zero (`TestApplied1KeepsAResultWithoutAllocating`).

#### Reproducibility envelope

> **Numbers vary across machines.** This report stamps the box that produced
> them so cross-machine deltas can be evaluated honestly. The box was shared
> with other builds while it ran: read ns/op as an order of magnitude, the
> allocation count as exact.

| Dimension | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU cores          | 10 (Apple M1 Pro) |
| RAM                | 16 GiB |
| OS / kernel        | Darwin 25.6.0 |
| Architecture       | arm64 |
| Go toolchain       | go1.27.3 darwin/arm64 |
| Git branch         | `feat/sdk-lot-1-c-loop` |
| Git commit         | `8219ffc28` (pre-commit) |
| Generated (UTC)    | 2026-11-12 |
| Bench wall-clock   | `-test.benchtime=1s`, single run |
| Fixture            | one forward outstanding (`keepResults = 1`), one caller parked at index 2^62, nil results |

#### Results

```
BenchmarkApplied1WithAForwardOutstanding-10    	83174492	        17.58 ns/op	       0 B/op	       0 allocs/op
```

#### Reading

- **0 allocs/op** per applied command of a nil result with a forward
  outstanding: one store into the ring slot `index % 4096`, and one look at
  the head of the waiter heap, which holds a caller not yet due.
- Before #1109 the same entry wrote the `results` map, appended to
  `resultOrder` and, past 4 096 entries, deleted the oldest and resliced its
  head, then broadcast to every parked caller.

| Followers | Side | turn p99 (six runs) | median | turn p50 (median) | commit p99 (range) |

- **The turn p99 moved by less than its own spread**: the two sides' six
  runs overlap entirely, and no round moves it by more than the spread of

  (a7eb89f0d), not the parent of #912's commit, whose tests do not build.
- **The median turn is some 10 % longer after the lot** (4.14 to 4.58 µs,
  3.46 to 3.84 µs), every after run above every before run. That is lot L1
  as a whole, measured through a whole turn; the encoding it cut is the
  smaller part of a turn that sends nothing big, and this bench does not
  say which other change of the lot added the 0.4 µs.

### Commit p99 while a snapshot streams (#920, #1365)

From `streamcommit_bench_test.go`; refresh with `cd internal && go test -run='^$' -bench=BenchmarkACommitWhileASnapshotStreams -benchtime=1x -count=5 -v ./service/app/consensus/` (`-v` prints each window's seconds).
#920's third criterion: the data lane's commit p99 while a paced stream
runs, within 10 % of the no-stream baseline. Three voters over loopback
mutual TLS with memory logs, a state of six seconds of stream (values of
4 KiB of random bytes, so that #917's compression leaves its size: 12 MiB
at 2 MiB/s, 48 MiB at 8 MiB/s), cut once when loaded and never in a
window; then three windows of 4 s at 1 000 proposals/s of 256 B: with no
stream, then from the first byte a fourth node that JOINed as a learner
is streamed the snapshot at the rate `SnapshotStreamBytesPerSecond` names
(the run fails unless the stream is still in flight at the window's
end), then once the learner installed it and follows. One run is one new
cluster. Taken 2026-11-13 on devbox (AMD EPYC 7351P, 8 cores, Linux
6.12.101 amd64, go1.27.4), `GOMAXPROCS=4`, five runs a rate.

| Rate | baseline p99 | streaming p99 | following p99 | ratio streaming / baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 MiB/s | 1.362 – 1.405 ms | 1.390 – 1.425 ms | 1.404 – 1.477 ms | 1.014, 1.000, 1.022, 1.020, 1.028 |
| 8 MiB/s | 1.382 – 5.576 ms | 1.416 – 6.234 ms | 1.423 – 4.893 ms | 4.105, 1.118, 0.994, 0.683, 1.024 |

- **At 2 MiB/s the bound holds** in every run: the stream moves the p99 by
  at most 2.8 %.
- **At 8 MiB/s this bench cannot judge it.** Stalls of 10 to 20 ms land
  in some seconds of every kind of window, the baseline and the window
  after the stream included (`-v`'s per-second lines): two runs of five
  are dominated by them, one each way. The four nodes share one process,
  one heap of four 48 MiB states and its four Ps, and the learner's
  receiving side runs on the leader's CPUs, which no deployment does. The
  stalls are not attributed here; the three quiet runs are within 2.4 %.
- An exploratory variant that let a cut of the 48 MiB state land in a
  window measured a p99 of 118 and 121 ms there: a cut, not a stream, is
  what a window must not hold, so the bench sizes `SnapshotEveryBytes` to
  cut once, before the windows.
